title: High Plains Agricultural Storage
content: Hay and implement storage outside Levelland, replacing an older structure that had been patched one winter too many. The operation needed the building standing before cutting started, which set the whole schedule and shaped most of the decisions on it. Category: AgriculturalLocation: Levelland, TexasBuilding Size: 18,400 sq ft
pageTitle: High Plains Agricultural Storage

title: Products Supplied
content: FS-A36 roofing and wall panelsVentilation packageFramed openingsFasteners and sealants FS-A36 throughout, roof and walls, cut to length off the rafter dimensions so there were no horizontal laps on the roof runs. On a building that stores hay, a lap is a place for water to find its way in eventually, and removing them entirely was worth more than the small premium on custom lengths. Ventilation drove the rest. Stored hay gives off heat and moisture, and a sealed metal box over it is a poor idea. Ridge ventilation runs the length of the building, and the south elevation was left open for implement access — which conveniently doubles as intake. That combination was settled during planning rather than retrofitted, which is the only sensible time to settle it. Framed openings on the enclosed elevations were detailed to the equipment the operation actually runs, not to a catalog size. The fastener and sealant package shipped complete with the panels — on a rural site an hour from the nearest supplier, a missing box of closures costs a day. Panels showed up cut to length, so there was no fighting laps on the roof. We were closed in before first cutting, which is all I asked for.Wade BennettBennett Ag Construction

title: Products Supplied
content: Pre-engineered building packageInsulated wall panelsStanding-seam roofingLoading-canopy components FS-I40 insulated wall panels carry the envelope. On a conditioned building this size, a panel that arrives as structure, insulation, and finished face in one piece removes an entire trade from the wall elevation and two weeks of sequencing from the schedule. The roof is FS-S16 standing seam in 24 gauge. On a low-slope roof of this footprint there is no argument for putting fasteners through the roof plane — the clips let the panel move with the temperature swing, and there is nothing exposed up there for anyone to come back and service. The dock elevation runs long, and the canopy framing was detailed around the door spacing the operator's own equipment needed rather than a standard bay. Material shipped in staged loads keyed to the erector's sequence, so the site was never storing more steel than it had room for. title: Products Supplied
content: FS-R36 roofing panelsFS-U36 wall panelsCustom trim packageStructural framing components FS-R36 went on the roof at 26 gauge — the purlin spacing on the frame made that the sensible call, and the owner wanted a roof he could walk on during installation without thinking about it. Walls are FS-U36, whose closer rib spacing keeps a long elevation looking tidy from the county road it faces. The trim package took the most work. Two of the overhead door openings sit close enough to a corner that standard jamb trim would have left a gap, so we formed those pieces to the dimensions on the framing drawings rather than asking the crew to improvise on site. The wainscot band was a late addition and cost very little once the trim was already being run. Materials went out bundled by elevation and labeled, which on a four-person crew with no lift on site is the difference between a good week and a frustrating one. The building has been in daily use since it closed in. They caught two door trim conditions I had not thought about and formed the pieces before the order shipped. title: Westline Service Facility
content: A fleet service facility in Abilene, built for a maintenance operation that works on heavy equipment year-round. Buildings like this get used hard — traffic in and out all day, equipment moving through the bays, walls that get bumped. The specification reflected that from the start. Category: IndustrialLocation: Abilene, TexasBuilding Size: 22,750 sq ft
pageTitle: Westline Service Facility

title: Products Supplied
content: Structural framingRoof and wall panelsInterior liner panelsCustom formed trim FS-R36 in 24 gauge on roof and walls. On a working facility this is where the heavier gauge earns itself back — not in any single dramatic way, but in a decade of doors slamming, equipment brushing past, and nobody being precious about the building. Inside, FS-L29 liner panels run through the service bays. The maintenance crew wanted a surface they could hose down rather than something that absorbs a decade of grease and diesel. Liner also brightens the bays considerably, which matters when someone is under a machine with a flashlight. The equipment bay openings are wider than standard, and where the framing met the existing yard wall there was no catalog trim that fit. Those pieces were formed to submitted dimensions on our press brake — a small part of the order that would have cost the crew a full day of improvising had it not been there. The custom flashing where we tied into the old yard wall fit first time. That is not something I take for granted on a retrofit condition.Daniel MercerMercer Building Systems
